system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “FINAL”, “market standard” and “principal-level agreement” statements are **Seller assertions, not evidence of Buyer approval**. The positions below are Buyer negotiation recommendations, not agreed terms. Review is based on the supplied extracts; the underlying SPA and DD documents have not been independently verified.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery proportionate to exposure, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m as an opening position**, subject to DD and recovery security; a 20% cap leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000** individually and **AUD 250,000** collectively; only the excess over the basket is recoverable. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims and a tipping basket; exclusions for protected claim categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated and separate-category exclusions; the proposed deductible permanently strands otherwise valid losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties, with separately negotiated periods for other categories and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Seek 36 months and reject blanket application**; latent issues may emerge after 18 months and different claim types require different periods. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | Separate warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership, valid issue and unencumbered transfer; no basket/de minimis, a price-level cap and materially longer survival. | **Require a separate regime: at least 100% of price and a six-year contractual notification period**, subject to applicable limitation law; Buyer must have meaningful recourse if it does not receive the ownership purchased. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is identified. | Express preservation of remedies for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, with attribution carefully defined and legally non-excludable rights preserved. | **Carve fraud out across every relevant limitation, release, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clause**; Buyer should not depend on litigation over whether contractual protections shield dishonest conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Only matters fairly disclosed in sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope should qualify identified warranties; a frozen, indexed disclosure record. | **Reject blanket disclosure and require specific, adequately detailed disclosures**, with any general disclosures narrowly agreed; mere document availability should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer **or its advisers**, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | No knowledge exclusion; alternatively, only actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer decision-makers at signing, without constructive or adviser-imputed knowledge. | **Delete the qualifier or narrow it strictly, preserving specific indemnities**; “discoverable” knowledge effectively makes Buyer warrant the completeness of its own diligence. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure confirms no final consent or evidence of satisfied associated conditions. | A Buyer-waivable condition precedent requiring valid consent and satisfaction of relevant contractual conditions, without unacceptable amendments or costs. | **Keep Bluefen as a substantive completion condition, with evidence of compliance with clauses 11.2–11.3**; written consent alone may not protect a customer representing approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Verified payout, repayment through the completion funds flow and effective discharge of all relevant security, guarantees and obligations at Completion. | **Require a binding payout/release arrangement effective at Completion and deduct debt under the price mechanics**; Buyer should not pay a debt-free price while inheriting secured debt or relying on a later release. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** of conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable employer on-costs, including amounts payable after Completion; clear treatment of conditions and payment responsibility. | **Quantify and expressly allocate these amounts to Seller through an agreed adjustment, funded payment or indemnity, without double counting**; omission otherwise leaves Buyer funding transaction-related employment liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; transfer is payment-conditioned, AUD 180,000 remains recorded as open, and payment/assignment evidence is absent. | Verified payment and effective chain of title to all relevant materials, plus protection against ownership, infringement, remediation and business-interruption losses arising from the identified matter. | **Require payment evidence and an effective confirmatory assignment before Completion, backed by a broader specific indemnity outside general warranty limits**; covering only the invoice does not cure uncertain IP ownership. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; access, scope and notification obligations remain unresolved. | Prompt forensic and legal investigation, containment, evidence preservation, lawful notification assessment, updates and protection against pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require investigation and remediation covenants plus a specific indemnity, with completion protection if findings are material**; the incident is unresolved—not a confirmed notifiable breach, but not safely dismissible either. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure does not establish timing, avoidability, accrual or ordinary-course status. | Review the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** commitment, service periods, cancellation rights and accounting treatment; control further commitments before Completion. | **Verify the related renewals together and allocate them under the agreed debt/working-capital and conduct provisions**; neither ordinary-course treatment nor a price deduction is justified without the underlying facts. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance extend to Claims of every nature. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental/title warranties, tax, specific indemnities, price/payment obligations, covenants and fraud, with tailored remedies and limitations. | **Create a category-by-category limitations schedule and override inconsistent catch-all wording**; otherwise negotiated protections can be neutralised by broad definitions and cross-references. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital and ownership against corporate records, issue/transfer history, certificates, shareholder arrangements, options and encumbrances; effective completion transfers. | **Verify title beyond the register and obtain full title warranties and completion deliverables**; the register is evidence, not a complete check of beneficial ownership, competing rights or security. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Seller treats tax and IP warranties as settled under the general regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion liabilities, appropriately longer tax survival, and robust IP ownership, assignment, licensing and infringement protection. | **Keep tax and IP expressly open pending full drafting and DD**, negotiating tailored caps, periods and exclusions; Seller’s assertion of settlement does not resolve these distinct risks, and the Ironquay indemnity is no substitute for broader IP protection. |

**Buyer priority:** resolve Bluefen, Riverlark and IP ownership before Completion; settle the bonus funds-flow treatment; and prevent the general limitations from swallowing separately negotiated protections.
=== END ADVICE ===
